title: Connect pass payload
description: The payload of a connect pass, the exact JSON bytes the control plane signed. Its members come in no set order: the pass carries the exact bytes signed, and the adapter parses those bytes. A connect pass is the payload in base64url without padding, a dot, and the signature in base64url without padding, at most 1024 characters with no white space; the signature is 64 bytes of Ed25519 under the control plane's server key over qory-connect-ed25519-v1, a line feed and the payload bytes. The control plane sends a person to the adapter's connect_url (adapter.schema.json) with the pass as the query parameter state. The adapter sends the page that receives the pass with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, so the pass leaves in no Referer header. The adapter decodes the pass strictly, both parts as strict base64url without padding, and verifies the signature under a server key the adapter pinned at enrolment: after a server key rotation it tries each pinned key, and any one that verifies passes. It then reads the payload against this schema, checks that adapter_id is the id the adapter is enrolled as, and refuses a pass whose expires_at has passed on its clock, or is more than 15 minutes ahead of it; expires_at bounds only the pass's arrival at the adapter, not the person's round trip at the source. An adapter accepts a connect pass once: it records the nonce in one atomic check-and-insert, so the first browser to bring the pass wins, and a second arrival of the same pass is refused on the adapter's page, and the adapter mints no connect return for it. It keeps the nonce, in storage that survives a restart, until expires_at has passed on its clock. connection_id names the connection the person is making; connection_id in definitions.schema.json says when it is made. After its checks, the adapter links the access the source grants to that connection_id. Access the source grants without a connect pass links nothing. The adapter links a grant only when the source confirms it for this flow. The person authorised the grant at the source during this flow, and the source returned it to the same flow that carries the pass. When it accepts the pass, the adapter makes a random state value of at least 128 bits for this pass, and keeps the pass on its side, bound to the browser by a short-lived cookie it sets. The pass never leaves the adapter: the adapter sends the source only that state value, never the pass, and never logs the pass. On the source's return, the adapter accepts the grant only when the state value and the browser's cookie both match the same accepted pass, and it checks with the source, under the authorisation the person gave at the source, that this person administers the account the grant belongs to at the source, not merely can read it. It signs linked only for a grant finished in that browser, under that exact pass. It never links a grant identified only by a value the browser sends back. A grant is linked to at most one live connection. A grant already linked to another live connection is refused until that connection ends (connections-disconnect.schema.json). So the race rule ends another connection's collection only when the source has really moved the collection between grants (source-collections.schema.json). A link that is pending, its connection not yet made, is replaced by a later flow, never refused grant_taken, and the adapter drops it once the connect return it minted for it has expired, as definitions.schema.json says; grant_taken is only for a grant live under another connection. Every flow checks again that the person administers the account. The adapter learns a connection is made when a listing naming it is answered 204 rather than 403. The adapter hands the result back to the control plane in a connect return (connect-return.schema.json). A connect return of any outcome spends the pass: after a refused or cancelled return, the person starts connecting again from the control plane and gets a new pass. The control plane makes a connection only when the return arrives in the browser session of the person who started connecting. An adapter cannot tell whose pass it holds, so it relies on that check.

adapter_id.description: The adapter the pass is for, as the control plane enrolled it.

connection_id.description: The connection the person is making, as the control plane issued it. The adapter links the access the source grants to it, and names it in source-collections.schema.json.

nonce.description: 128 random bits in base64url without padding, 22 characters, new for each pass.

expires_at.description: When the pass expires, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds, at most 15 minutes after the control plane issued it. The adapter refuses a pass whose expires_at has passed on its clock, or is more than 15 minutes ahead of it, and keeps the pass's nonce until expires_at has passed. It bounds only the pass's arrival at the adapter, not the person's round trip at the source.
